text: Machiavelli judged every ruler by one thing. Not his words.
"The first opinion which one forms of a prince, and of his understanding, is by observing the men he has around him."
Capable, loyal people beside you, and the world calls you wise. Weak ones, and it starts to doubt you.
He saw three kinds of minds. One works things out alone. One understands when shown. One does neither.
The first is excellent. The second is good. The third, in his word, useless.
Flatterers? His only guard: let people know the truth won't offend you.
But not everyone. Pick a few trusted, clear-thinking people and let them speak freely when you ask.
